title: Grand Theft Auto 2/Gangs
text:
Each Area is divided between neutral territory, and that for three gangs: two local, and one active in all three districts (so seven in total).

When you start play or are otherwise in neutral territory, colored arrow markers point to the public blue phone in each gang's territory, at least while there's still a job to be completed for that gang. If a phone is ringing and its booth flashing, run over to it to answer: the caller's face appears to the bottom left, and the  is shown in text along the bottom of the screen.

Once you enter a gang's territory, these markers can be replaced by others pointing to gang phones with at least one job to offer to those who answer it if they have enough respect, the color of the notch of each arrow showing the phone's color.

You start play able to accept jobs offered at green phones, one at each phone.There are only two yellow phones but three jobs, the third of which can only be started after completing one of the first two. Similarly, there's only one red phone but two jobs, the second of which can only started after completing the first.

Answering a phone can start a job, at which point you cannot save status or start another job until that already active had been failed or completed. Failure loses some respect from that gang, but as long as you still have enough respect you can answer the same phone and try again. Completing a job earns some respect from that gang, paying a bonus and increasing Bonus Multiplier by 1, while any  level is removed.

Respect with each gang in an area is shown by three meters in the top left corner of the screen, showing gang signs and colors:

Colored lights along the bottom of each meter show which phones have been unlocked with enough respect, even once their jobs have been completed.

Each gang uses a distinctive vehicle with the gang sign on its rooftop, driven by an armed gang member. These signs can also be seen in a gang's territory, on buildings or rooftops, or on gantries spanning the streets below as you enter and move around. Gang members, both armed and unarmed, walk the streets of their territory wearing gang colors.

If a gang has any respect for you, then you can enter its territory without being attacked, and its members can assist you if you're attacked by others. Running down or killing gang members may lose the respect of that gang, but its members will still ignore or assist you as long as that gang still has any respect for you: only once you have negative respect will you be attacked.

However, gaining enough respect with one gang to unlock its other phones, and jobs which pay higher bonuses, normally means losing the respect of its rival in equal but opposite measure.

All's well if a job doesn't involve entering rival territory, but if it does then it can make completing that job more difficult: not only do rival gang members become more aggressive, but in Areas 2-3 they can switch to more deadly weapons once below certain thresholds of disrespect.

Respect has its limits, though: once at maximum with a gang, the positive sign (+) on the right end of its meter flashes, while once at minimum, the negative sign (-) on the left end does so. Once at maximum or minimum respect, no more can be gained or lost.

There's one way to gain respect with one gang while not losing it with another: take a specific vehicle to a gang's crusher, exit to let it be picked up and crushed, then pick up the  power-up from that crusher's conveyor belt.

In Area 1, there are five parked Wellards, and others driving. In Areas 2-3, Special Agent Cars appear at Wanted level 5, forming roadblocks and driving.
